evidence: Receiving online DO at 51.8h = 1.73 mg/L (receiving_observations row 259), below the 2 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO declined 2.58 -> 2.10 -> 1.73 mg/L over t=47.8-51.8h, an accelerating downward trend that KEEP cannot meet
Receiving P assay at 47.8h = 2.72 g/L, still rising (rows 259 P-assay), so continued operation retains product mass unlike stop
allowed_actions: strong_feed_reduction = [0.6, 1.15], the largest simultaneous OUR cut and OTR gain among non-stop plans
submission.rationale: Receiving DO fell abruptly at ~46h and has declined continuously, reaching 1.73 mg/L at 51.8h — already below the 2 mg/L hard limit. KEEP and mild interventions (reduce_feed or increase_air alone, or the 0.8/1.15 combined plan) do not give sufficient predicted margin against the still-falling trajectory given the hard-constraint priority. Strong feed reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) cuts feed-driven oxygen demand ~40% while raising oxygen transfer 15%, providing the widest feasible margin. It retains accumulated product mass (P ≈ 2.7 g/L and rising) and continues counted production, unlike a stop. Source batches (which stayed >8 mg/L DO) confirm this is a receiving-specific deviation, so source-calibrated extrapolation of DO recovery is not justified.
submission.uncertainty: No calibrated receiving-process physics model was available, so predicted DO response to feed/air changes is qualitative (OUR ∝ substrate uptake, DO ∝ OTR balance). Residual uncertainty: receiving OUR dynamics and model mismatch could delay DO recovery; however, the observed decline rate (~0.2 mg/L per 0.2h near the end) is large enough that only the strongest non-stop intervention is defensible against the hard constraint. If DO does not recover above 2 mg/L within the first hours post-decision, a stop would become necessary.
